question: How does an AI coding agent (Claude Code) produce the best three.js work: three.js-specific MCP servers/skills, LLM-oriented docs, version pitfalls per the official Migration Guide, and visual verification loops for rendered WebGL output?

claims.claim: threejs.org publishes an llms.txt at the site root that points to a fuller LLM doc index (docs/llms.txt) and a full inline dump including TSL (docs/llms-full.txt).
claims.quote: See the full documentation for LLMs at: https://threejs.org/docs/llms.txt

claims.claim: The official docs/llms.txt contains an explicit 'Instructions for Large Language Models' section; it labels an outdated import pattern WRONG and an import-map pattern CORRECT (import map observed pinning three@0.187.0 with 'three' -> build/three.module.js and 'three/addons/' -> examples/jsm/).
claims.quote: CORRECT - modern pattern (always use latest version):

claims.claim: The official LLM guidance names WebGLRenderer as the default, mature choice; WebGPURenderer is recommended only when TSL custom shaders, compute shaders or advanced node materials are needed.
claims.quote: **Use WebGLRenderer** (default, mature):

claims.claim: The official LLM guidance says custom materials under WebGPURenderer should be written in TSL, not raw GLSL.
claims.quote: When using WebGPURenderer, use TSL instead of raw GLSL for custom materials:

claims.claim: Context7 indexes three.js (mrdoob/three.js): 32,929 snippets and 2,999,570 tokens shown on the page, last update shown as '4 hours ago'; no version list was visible.
claims.quote: Three.js (mrdoob/three.js) | Context7

claims.claim: threejs-devtools-mcp (DmitriyGolub) is an MCP server that inspects and edits a live three.js scene; README states 69 tools; it works through a WebSocket bridge injected into a browser tab it opens; Claude Code install: `claude mcp add threejs-devtools-mcp -- npx threejs-devtools-mcp`. 130 GitHub stars on the page.
claims.quote: Three.js MCP server — inspect and edit scenes, materials, shaders, lights in real time from any AI agent

claims.claim: cloudai-x/threejs-skills is a set of 13 Claude Code skill files (fundamentals, geometry, materials, lighting, textures, animation, loaders, shaders, postprocessing, interaction, performance, react-three-fiber, asset-pipeline); install with `npx skills add cloudai-x/threejs-skills` or copy into ~/.claude/skills/ or .claude/skills/; 4.2k stars shown.
claims.quote: Skill files that give Claude Code current, verified knowledge of three.js

claims.claim: The cloudai-x skills are pinned to three.js r186, so they are one or two releases behind the Migration Guide's newest heading (187 -> 188) and the docs/llms.txt import map (0.187.0).
claims.quote: The skills target three.js r186 (`three@0.186`)

claims.claim: Color-space pitfall (r152): renderer.outputEncoding no longer exists; the property is outputColorSpace. LLM code using outputEncoding / sRGBEncoding is pre-r152.
claims.quote: `WebGLRenderer.outputEncoding` has been replaced with `WebGLRenderer.outputColorSpace`

claims.claim: Color-space pitfall (r152): texture.encoding became texture.colorSpace and the constant sRGBEncoding became SRGBColorSpace; ColorManagement is enabled by default from the same release.
claims.quote: `THREE.sRGBEncoding` is now `THREE.SRGBColorSpace`.

claims.claim: Color management default (r152), under heading '151 -> 152'.
claims.quote: `THREE.ColorManagement.enabled` is now `true` by default.

claims.claim: Lighting pitfall (r155): physically based light units are the default; light intensities copied from pre-r155 tutorials render differently (too dark/bright). Heading '154 -> 155'.
claims.quote: `WebGLRenderer.useLegacyLights` is now set to `false` by default and deprecated.

claims.claim: Lighting pitfall (r150): the old flag physicallyCorrectLights was renamed, so code setting renderer.physicallyCorrectLights is stale. Heading '149 -> 150'.
claims.quote: `WebGLRenderer.physicallyCorrectLights = true` is now `WebGLRenderer.useLegacyLights = false`.

claims.claim: Entry-point pitfall (r171): WebGPURenderer and NodeMaterial classes import from 'three/webgpu', TSL functions from 'three/tsl', not from 'three'. Heading '170 -> 171'.
claims.quote: Use `three/webgpu` to import modules related to `WebGPURenderer` and `NodeMaterial`.

claims.claim: The r171 release notes record the WebGL/WebGPU entry-point code split (PRs #29404, #29644) and the new three.tsl.js build (PR #29948).
claims.quote: Codesplit WebGL/WebGPU entrypoints.

claims.claim: Addons pitfall (r148): loaders and controls exist only as ES modules under examples/jsm (examples/js script-tag builds are gone). Heading '147 -> 148'.
claims.quote: Addons like `GLTFLoader` or `OrbitControls` are now only available as ES6 modules in the `examples/jsm` directory.

claims.claim: Build pitfall (r161): the non-module builds were removed, so `<script src=.../build/three.min.js>` with a global THREE fails on current releases. Heading '160 -> 161'.
claims.quote: The build files `build/three.js` and `build/three.min.js` have been removed.

claims.claim: WebGL 1 pitfall (r163): WebGLRenderer is WebGL 2 only. Heading '162 -> r163'.
claims.quote: `WebGLRenderer` no longer supports WebGL 1.

claims.claim: WebGPU/TSL churn examples: TSL varying() renamed in r173 (heading '172 -> 173'); PostProcessing class renamed RenderPipeline in r183 (heading '182 -> 183'). TSL/WebGPU API names change release to release, raising LLM error risk.
claims.quote: `PostProcessing` has been renamed to `RenderPipeline`.

claims.claim: TSL rename in r173, heading '172 -> 173'.
claims.quote: The TSL function `varying()` has been renamed to `toVarying()`.

claims.claim: renderer.info is the official source for per-frame draw calls and triangle counts plus live geometry/texture counts; an agent can read it via page.evaluate. Fields quoted on the page: render.calls 'The number of draw calls per frame.', render.triangles, memory.geometries, memory.textures. With multi-pass rendering set renderer.info.autoReset = false and call renderer.info.reset() per frame.
claims.quote: Holds a series of statistical information about the GPU memory and the rendering process. Useful for debugging and monitoring.

claims.claim: Headless Chrome on a GPU-less machine no longer falls back to software WebGL automatically; the documented opt-in flag set is `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader-webgl --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`.
claims.quote: Allowing automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader has been deprecated.

claims.claim: Playwright MCP defaults to accessibility snapshots, which carry no information about canvas pixels; for WebGL the agent must call browser_take_screenshot explicitly (coordinate-based vision tools are opt-in via --caps=vision). Claude Code install: `claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest`.
claims.quote: Take a screenshot of the current page. Use browser_snapshot for actions by default.

claims.claim: chrome-devtools-mcp is an alternative verification channel: screenshots via take_screenshot (CLI example `chrome-devtools take_screenshot 1 --filePath screenshot.png`) and performance traces; installed in Claude Code as a plugin (`/plugin marketplace add ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`, `/plugin install chrome-devtools-mcp@chrome-devtools-plugins`).
claims.quote: Your MCP client should open the browser and record a performance trace.
